extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate or beginning graduate students learning algebraic topology (homology theory)
extracted.subtask_description: Section of a textbook developing the relationship between simplicial and singular homology, proving excision, naturality, equivalence of simplicial and singular homology, degree theory for maps S^n→S^n, and introducing cellular homology. Contains definitions, constructions, and proofs used to compute and reason about homology groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barycentric subdivision operator S is a chain map
rubrics_metrics.description: Define S : C_n(X) → C_n(X) by Sσ = σ_♯ S_n where S_n is the signed sum of the n simplices in the barycentric subdivision of Δ^n; the operator S is a chain map since ∂Sσ = S∂σ (i.e., ∂σ_♯S_n = σ_♯∂S_n = σ_♯S_{n−1}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly: for a singular n-simplex σ, Sσ is the corresponding signed sum of the restrictions of σ to the n simplices of the barycentric subdivision of Δ^n. The displayed face-wise calculation verifies ∂S = S∂. Use the subdivision operator when refining chains to lie in fine covers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of chain homotopy T between S and identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Define T : C_n(X) → C_{n+1}(X) by Tσ = σ_♯ T_n and this gives a chain homotopy between S and the identity since ∂T + T∂ = 1 − S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The verification is via the computation ∂Tσ = σ − Sσ − T(∂σ). Use T derived from a prism/cone-type construction on simplices; the displayed calculation shows replacement of S by T in analogous steps. T is taken zero on certain subgroups (e.g., LC_{−1}(Y)) where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterated barycentric subdivision chain homotopy D_m = Σ_{0≤i<m} T S^i
rubrics_metrics.description: A chain homotopy between the identity and the iterate S^m is given by D_m = Σ_{i=0}^{m−1} T S^i because ∂D_m + D_m∂ = 1 − S^m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute ∂D_m + D_m∂ = Σ(∂T S^i + T S^i∂) = Σ(1 − S)S^i = 1 − S^m. Use D_m to relate iterated subdivision to the identity chain-wise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of a Lebesgue number for compact metric spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: For an open cover of a compact metric space there exists ε > 0 such that every set of diameter less than ε lies in some set of the cover (a Lebesgue number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to guarantee that for each singular simplex σ there exists m large enough so that simplices of S^m(σ) have diameter < ε and hence lie in some element of the cover; standard compactness argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of m(σ) to place subdivided simplex in a cover
rubrics_metrics.description: For each singular n-simplex σ define m(σ) to be the smallest m such that S^m σ lies in C_n^U(X) (i.e., the chain supported in elements of the cover U).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: m(σ) may vary with σ; use it to define D: C_n(X)→C_{n+1}(X) by Dσ = D_{m(σ)}σ where D_{m} = Σ_{0≤i<m} T S^i. This construction produces chain homotopies tailored to local refinements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of ρ = 1 − ∂D − D∂ as a chain map into C_n^U(X)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define ρ = 1 − ∂D − D∂. Then ρ is a chain map with image in C_n^U(X) and satisfies the chain homotopy equation ∂D + D∂ = 1 − ρ. Moreover, ρ restricted to C_n^U(X) is the identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify ∂ρ(σ) = ∂σ − ∂^2 Dσ − ∂D∂σ = ∂σ − ∂D∂σ, and ρ(∂σ) equals the same, showing chain map property. Expand ρ(σ) as σ − ∂Dσ − D∂σ = S^{m(σ)}σ + D_{m(σ)}(∂σ) − D(∂σ), and argue terms lie in C_n^U(X) using monotonicity of m on faces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excision theorem via chain-level homotopies
rubrics_metrics.description: For a decomposition X = A ∪ B and cover U = {A, B} define C_n(A + B) as sums of chains in A and in B. The inclusion C_n(A + B)/C_n(A) → C_n(X)/C_n(A) induces an isomorphism on homology; consequently H_n(B, A∩B) ≈ H_n(X, A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All maps appearing in the chain homotopy formulas take chains in A to chains in A and induce quotient maps with the same homotopy relations; identify quotient groups with free abelian groups generated by singular simplices in B not lying in A to produce the isomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient map q induces isomorphism for good pairs (Proposition 2.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (X,A) is a good pair then the quotient map q : (X,A) → (X/A, A/A) induces isomorphisms q_* : H_n(X,A) → H_n(X/A, A/A) ≈ H_n(X/A) for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses a neighborhood V of A which deformation retracts onto A; apply long exact sequences of triples and excision to get commutative diagram with three isomorphisms making q_* an isomorphism. Good pairs ensure H_n(V,A)=0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative homology as reduced absolute homology via cone/mapping cone
rubrics_metrics.description: For arbitrary pairs (X,A) there is an isomorphism H_n(X,A) ≈ H_n(X ∪ C A) (where C A is the cone on A) obtained by the sequence of isomorphisms H_n(X ∪ C A) ≈ H_n(X ∪ C A, C A) ≈ H_n(X ∪ C A − {p}, C A − {p}) ≈ H_n(X,A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contractibility of C A, excision, and deformation retraction of C A − {p} onto A to establish the chain of isomorphisms; this realizes relative homology as reduced absolute homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit cycles representing generators of H_n(D^n, ∂D^n) and H_n(S^n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the single characteristic map of Δ^n (viewed as singular n-simplex) as a relative cycle generating H_n(D^n, ∂D^n); inductively construct generators for H_n(S^n) by decomposing S^n into two n-simplices with identified boundaries, and following boundary maps in long exact sequences of pairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For n>0 use isomorphisms H_n(Δ^n, ∂Δ^n) ≈ H_{n−1}(∂Δ^n, ...) and identifications to transport generators; show explicit chains like Δ_n^1 − Δ_n^2 represent generator of H_n(S^n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excision for subcomplexes of CW complexes (Corollary 2.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a CW complex X is union of subcomplexes A and B then inclusion (B, A∩B) → (X,A) induces isomorphisms H_n(B, A∩B) → H_n(X,A) for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since CW pairs are good, apply Proposition 2.22 to pass to quotient spaces and note homeomorphisms of quotients (assuming nontrivial intersection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wedge sum homology is direct sum of summands (Corollary 2.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a wedge sum ∨_α X_α formed at basepoints x_α with pairs (X_α, x_α) good, the inclusions i_α : X_α → ∨_α X_α induce an isomorphism ⊕_α i_{α*} : ⊕_α H_n(X_α) → H_n(∨_α X_α).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reduced homology equivalence to homology relative to basepoint and apply Proposition 2.22.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invariance of dimension via local homology (Theorem 2.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: If nonempty open sets U ⊂ R^m and V ⊂ R^n are homeomorphic then m = n, because for x ∈ U the local homology H_k(U, U − {x}) ≈ H_k(R^m, R^m − {x}) is Z for k = m and 0 otherwise, and homeomorphisms preserve these groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use excision and the long exact sequence for the pair (R^m, R^m − {x}) and the deformation retraction R^m − {x} ≃ S^{m−1} to compute local homology. Compare dimensions via homology concentration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and invariance of local homology groups H_n(X, X−{x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Local homology groups at x are H_n(X, X − {x}); for any open neighborhood U of x, excision gives H_n(X, X−{x}) ≈ H_n(U, U−{x}) provided points are closed, so these groups depend only on local topology and are preserved by homeomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local homology to detect local non-homeomorphism; homeomorphisms induce isomorphisms H_n(X, X−{x}) → H_n(Y, Y−{f(x)}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturality of long exact sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Long exact sequences (e.g., of a pair, triple, reduced homology, or coming from a short exact sequence of chain complexes) are natural: maps induced by f : (X,A) → (Y,B) make the corresponding long exact sequence diagrams commute, and boundary maps satisfy f_∗ ∂ = ∂ f_∗.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commutativity can be checked at chain level: f_# ∂ = ∂ f_#; or appeal to the general algebraic fact that the long exact sequence induced by a short exact sequence of chain complexes is natural. Use this to transfer homological relations across maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of simplicial and singular homology (Theorem 2.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a (Δ) complex X with subcomplex A, the canonical homomorphisms H_Δ^n(X,A) → H_n(X,A) (from simplicial to singular homology) are isomorphisms for all n and all complex pairs (X,A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof first for finite-dimensional X and A empty via induction on skeleta and Five-Lemma, then extend to infinite-dimensional using compactness of supports of cycles (compact sets meet only finitely many open simplices) and to pairs via the five-lemma applied to long exact sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-Lemma (algebraic criterion for isomorphism)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a commutative diagram of abelian groups with two exact rows, if α, β, δ, ε are isomorphisms then γ is an isomorphism. Surjectivity/injectivity parts: (a) γ surjective if β, δ surjective and ε injective; (b) γ injective if β, δ injective and α surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses diagram chasing: start with element in target and lift/back-solve via exactness and isomorphism hypotheses. Frequently quoted and used to deduce middle-map isomorphisms in long exact sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite generation of homology for finite complexes; Betti numbers and torsion
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a finite Δ-complex with finitely many n-simplices then H_n(X) is finitely generated; writing it as a direct sum of cyclic groups, the number of Z summands is the n-th Betti number and the finite cyclic summands give torsion coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows since simplicial chain groups are finitely generated and so are their subgroups of cycles and quotient homology groups; classical computational viewpoint via boundary maps yields Betti numbers/torsion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of a map f : S^n → S^n via induced homomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: For n>0 the induced map f_* : H_n(S^n) → H_n(S^n) is multiplication by an integer d; this integer is deg f. Basic properties: deg 1 = 1; deg f = 0 if f not surjective; homotopy invariant; multiplicative under composition; deg of reflection = −1; antipodal map degree = (−1)^{n+1}; maps without fixed points have degree (−1)^{n+1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use H_n(S^n) ≈ Z and algebraic properties of induced maps; many topological consequences follow (e.g., degree detects surjectivity, fixed-point related constraints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Using degree to study vector fields and group actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications: (Theorem 2.28) S^n has a continuous nonzero tangent vector field iff n is odd (proof via homotopy between identity and antipodal map). (Proposition 2.29) If n is even then Z_2 is the only nontrivial group that can act freely on S^n (argument via degree homomorphism G → {±1}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate geometric constructions to homotopies and compute degrees; use multiplicative and parity properties of degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local degree and sum formula for degree (Proposition 2.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f : S^n → S^n and for some y the preimage f^{-1}(y) = {x_1,...,x_m} is finite, then deg f = Σ_i deg(f |_{x_i}) where deg(f |_{x_i}) is the local degree at x_i computed via excision and identifications H_n(U_i, U_i − {x_i}) ≈ Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct small disjoint neighborhoods U_i of each x_i mapped into a neighborhood V of y and apply excision plus exact sequences; local degrees are often ±1 if f is locally a homeomorphism near x_i. Useful for explicit degree computations (e.g., maps z ↦ z^k on S^1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension preserves degree (Proposition 2.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: For f : S^n → S^n, the suspension S f : S^{n+1} → S^{n+1} satisfies deg(S f) = deg f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cone and quotient constructions Cf : (C S^n, S^n) → (C S^n, S^n) and naturality of boundary maps in long exact sequences of the pair (C S^n, S^n) to transport the multiplication factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of maps of any given degree (Examples 2.31,2.32)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any integer k (and n≥1) one can construct f : S^n → S^n of degree k by collapsing complements of k disjoint balls to a point and mapping the resulting wedge-sphere to a single sphere (choice of local signs gives ±1 contributions), or by suspending z ↦ z^k for S^1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose quotient map q : S^n → ∨_k S^n collapsing complements of k disjoint balls, then map ∨_k S^n → S^n identifying summands with chosen orientations to achieve desired sum of local degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cellular homology preliminaries (Lemma 2.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a CW complex then (a) H_k(X^n, X^{n−1}) = 0 for k ≠ n and is free abelian with basis corresponding to n-cells when k = n; (b) H_k(X^n) = 0 for k > n; (c) inclusion H_k(X^n) → H_k(X) is an isomorphism for k < n and surjective for k = n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the fact X^n/X^{n−1} is a wedge of n-spheres (one per n-cell) and apply long exact sequences of the pair (X^n, X^{n−1}) together with inductive skeleta arguments. These are the foundational facts to define cellular chain complexes and compute homology efficiently.
